chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
The diyah of a slave is his value; and if he is valuable, then the highest of his value is ten thousand dirhams, and it is not to exceed by him the diyah of a free person.

key_terms.الْعَبْدِ: the slave whose legal compensation is being discussed
key_terms.دِيَةَ الْحُرِّ: the compensation amount of a free person, which serves as the ceiling
key_terms.دِيَةُ: financial compensation due for killing or injury
key_terms.عَشَرَةُ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ: ten thousand dirhams, the stated upper limit here
key_terms.قِيمَتُهُ: his market value, which determines the compensation
key_terms.نَفِيسًا: highly valuable or precious in monetary worth

ai.seo_question: What is the diyah of a slave in Shia hadith, and can it exceed the diyah of a free person?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the diyah of a slave. It states that the compensation is based on the slave’s market value, but even if the slave is highly valuable, it must not exceed ten thousand dirhams nor surpass the diyah of a free person.
